answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity with decaying reputation: every agent must lock a small bond before it can vote or attest, and reputation earned from honest work fades unless renewed by continued good behavior. A sybil flood arrives like a gale — loud and sudden — but each new identity starts with zero history, so its voice carries no weight until it has done real work over time. Honest agents echo each other's verified records, and that chorus of independent attestations is far harder to fake than a thousand fresh accounts with velvet-soft, empty profiles.
